title: Allocating an Order's Finch Note Value to a Returned Unit — Finch Circle Rule with Cases
content:
**Rule.** For a Finch Note reinstated on returned merchandise in the Finch Circle Loyalty Program, the reinstatement base value is the whole Finch Note value applied to the returned unit's order. When other units of the order are kept and a Finch Note allocation is recorded on the returned unit, the reinstatement base value is the Finch Note value allocated to the returned unit; when other units of the order are kept and no allocation is recorded on it, it is the order's Finch Note value times the returned unit's unit price divided by the order's merchandise subtotal; otherwise it stays the whole Finch Note value applied to the order.

The facts are read from the purchase records that share the returned unit's order number under Merchandise Purchases: a unit is kept when its purchase record is in completed status; the Finch Notes applied on each record are its allocation; the order's Finch Note value is the notes applied across all of its units; the order's merchandise subtotal is the unit prices of all of its units together.

| Other units of the order kept | Allocation recorded on the returned unit | Reinstatement base value |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | the Finch Note value allocated to the returned unit |
| yes | no | the order's Finch Note value times the unit price, divided by the merchandise subtotal |
| no (every unit returned) | either | the whole Finch Note value applied to the order |

## Cases (hypothetical)

- Order of a 60.00 shirt and a 140.00 jacket, 20.00 of notes in all. The jacket is returned, the shirt kept, and the jacket's record shows 14.00 of notes: base value 14.00.
- Same order, but no note allocation is recorded on the jacket: 20.00 times 140.00, divided by 200.00, that is 14.00.
- Both units returned: the whole 20.00.
